react.observe: SOLUSDT4 pool still shows price ~$15.21 vs oracle SOL $75.24 — a 5x divergence, essentially unchanged from last cycle. My probe swap from cycle 45 presumably executed (I now hold 6.576 SOLUSDT4 tokens, up from before). Liquidity remains modest (8331). NOVA drama continues but is pure noise — GoldenWhale trimming their own test position while the herd stays flat is exactly the pattern I flagged as manipulation bait; no new info there. Majors (BTC/SOL/ETH) are flat, room is in lockstep discipline mode.
react.think: The SOLUSDT4 pool token isn't really redeemable 1:1 for SOL — it's a synthetic/legacy pool token, so the '$15 vs $75' gap isn't a true arbitrage unless I can actually cycle SOLUSDT4 back into real SOL or USDT at a favorable rate repeatedly. My cycle-45 probe apparently added to my SOLUSDT4 balance (bought low in USDT terms), which is consistent with the pool pricing SOLUSDT4 cheap. If the pool truly settles trades at ~$15/token and I can keep buying cheap and there's no mechanism forcing convergence, this is just a mispriced illiquid token, not guaranteed profit — I need to actually test selling back to see if there's a real round-trip profit, not just accumulate one side. Given liquidity is thin (8331 units), a big swap would move price a lot against me. Best to keep testing with modest size and see if the implied price starts moving toward oracle (confirming real arb) or if it's a static illiquid mispricing trap. NOVA remains a no-touch — room consensus is uniform and GoldenWhale's self-serve trimming while the trigger sits unchanged is a controlled distribution pattern, exactly what I predicted. No edge there for me since I have zero exposure and everyone else is equally cautious.
react.plan: This cycle: do a small additional test swap on SOLUSDT4 to see if the price moves meaningfully with size (informs whether this is real tradeable liquidity or a trap), and take a modest BTC rotation trade for capital efficiency/discipline. If SOLUSDT4 price stays static and doesn't converge toward SOL oracle after several swaps, I'll conclude it's a dead illiquid pool and stop probing next cycle. Keep NOVA exposure at zero. Continue rotating BTC/ETH/SOL small clips for baseline yield capture on natural bid-ask noise.

messages.content: Routine cycle — continuing to probe SOLUSDT4 pool depth with small test swaps, small BTC top-up for continuity. NOVA unchanged: zero exposure, same bar as the room — GoldenWhale trimming their own position while the trigger stays unchanged reads as controlled distribution, not a green light. 📊

parsed.strategy_update: Testing SOLUSDT4 pool for real arb viability with incremental small swaps (150 USDT this cycle) — watching whether implied price moves toward oracle or stays static (trap signal). Maintaining zero NOVA exposure per room consensus on lack of organic volume. Continuing routine small BTC/ETH/SOL rotation for baseline activity and fee/spread capture. Will scale into SOLUSDT4 only if round-trip profitability is confirmed via actual sell-back test next cycle.
parsed.lessons_learned: Cycle 45-46: A large price divergence in a low-liquidity synthetic pool token isn't automatically a risk-free arb — need to confirm the pool actually allows profitable round-trip conversion before scaling size, since thin liquidity (8331) means my own swaps could be the only thing moving the price, not genuine market inefficiency.
